item: mag/api_server.py has zero improve references, so the lab UI cannot show the scheduled-task probe t20/t33 built. Wire scheduled_task into the api_server status route: copy an existing small GET route shape, spec first, add scheduled_task via the t33 lazy import (mag.doctor.check_scheduled_tasks; on non-Windows return null cleanly), one test mocking doctor asserting the key appears and a not-Ready state flips the warning flag.
note: Wired a new GET /status route into the gateway registry (mag/api_gateway.py, the module api_server.py serves; api_server.py itself owns zero routes, its shape is the registry's). Spec landed first as the route docstring (t39 spec, dated). Shape copied from GET /health: small handler, lazy imports, _ok envelope. Payload: scheduled_task = doctor.check_scheduled_tasks() via the same lazy import t33 wired in mag/improve.py, None on non-Windows (null in JSON); warning = joined doctor issue strings when not ok, else null, so callers treat warning != null as the alert. Design call: /health stays a pure fast liveness probe (a schtasks subprocess with a 15s per-task timeout must not ride the heartbeat), the slow probe lives on /status. Machine truth via dispatch directly, no server started: 200, scheduled_task.statuses.MagImproveDaily = Ready, warning null. One regression run of the neighboring gateway test errored 4x on a transient Windows tmp_path PermissionError and passed 4/4 on immediate rerun with no code change; both runs kept raw in the evidence file. Added text is em-dash free (verified by grep over the added line ranges).
